findings.title: Resource lookups use the resource-server ID as the owner
findings.body: The third argument to `findByName` filters by resource owner, but schema-created resources are owned by `resourceServer.getClientId()` (see `AdminPermissionsSchema`). Passing `server.getId()` here means client-specific resources are not found; the equivalent lookup at line 244 also misses the all-clients resource. Consequently, V2 client permission checks cannot find their resources and authorized administrators are denied.

findings.title: All-clients grants are skipped when a client resource exists
findings.body: The all-clients resource is evaluated only when the individual client resource is absent. Once any permission creates an individual resource for a client, checks for other scopes evaluate only that client resource, so grants attached to the all-clients resource no longer apply to that client. For example, a client with an individual VIEW permission will not inherit a global MANAGE permission. Evaluate the all-clients grant independently of whether the individual resource exists.
